sense.definition: Pleasant and enjoyable.
sense.example: We spent an agreeable afternoon walking by the river.

originalSense.definition: Able to agree; possible to be agreed.
originalSense.example: The revised terms were agreeable to both parties.

reason: An obscure ability-to-agree definition and an acceptability example obscured the everyday pleasant meaning.

sense.definition: To change or develop gradually over time.
sense.example: The town evolved from a fishing village into a busy port.

originalSense.definition: To move (something) in regular procession through a system.
originalSense.example: The drill instructor evolved the troops through a series of formations.
originalSense.usage: Specialised or historical meaning; this learning example illustrates the existing selected sense, not its most common modern use.

reason: The military movement meaning is historical and unsuitable as the common first meaning.

sense.definition: Not immediately obvious or easy to notice or understand.
sense.example: There is a subtle difference between the two proposals.

originalSense.definition: Very fine or delicate in physical structure.
originalSense.example: The subtle particles were too fine to see without magnification.

reason: Dictionary candidates are broad tangible/intangible headings rather than an explicit learner sense; separate the modern not-obvious meaning from the fine-particle meaning.

sense.definition: An amount of money or another resource provided or permitted for a particular purpose.
sense.example: Employees receive a monthly travel allowance.

originalSense.definition: Permission; granting, conceding, or admitting.
originalSense.example: The council acted with the king's allowance.
originalSense.usage: Specialised or historical meaning; this learning example illustrates the existing selected sense, not its most common modern use.

reason: The old permission meaning should not be the modern learner default.

sense.definition: A period of ten years.
sense.example: The population has doubled over the past decade.

originalSense.definition: A group or set of ten things.
originalSense.example: The old text describes a decade of soldiers marching together.
originalSense.usage: Specialised or historical meaning; this learning example illustrates the existing selected sense, not its most common modern use.

reason: The candidate's decade-of-time example and decennium synonyms identify the ten-years sense despite its shortened definition; preserve the separate set-of-ten meaning.

sense.definition: The process of getting rid of something that is no longer needed.
sense.example: The council improved its system for waste disposal.

originalSense.definition: A disposition; an arrangement, categorization, or classification of things.
originalSense.example: The collection's disposal by subject made the books easier to locate.
originalSense.usage: Specialised or historical meaning; this learning example illustrates the existing selected sense, not its most common modern use.

reason: The arrangement meaning is rare; getting rid of waste is the useful modern default.

sense.definition: A person trained to design, build or maintain machines, structures or technical systems.
sense.example: The engineer checked the machinery before production began.

originalSense.definition: A soldier engaged in designing or constructing military works for attack or defence, or other engineering works.
originalSense.example: The army engineer designed a bridge for the troops to cross.

reason: The general engineering profession is more useful as a default than the military-only sense.

sense.definition: A person, thing or case that does not follow a general rule or is not included in it.
sense.example: Most shops close on Sunday, but the supermarket is an exception.

originalSense.definition: The act of excepting or excluding; exclusion; restriction by taking out something which would otherwise be included, as in a class, statement, rule.
originalSense.example: The exception of the final chapter leaves the argument incomplete.
wordFamily: there is an exception to every rule

reason: The excluded case meaning is the common learner meaning; the act-of-exclusion meaning remains separate.

sense.definition: An organised event or series of events celebrating music, culture or another theme.
sense.example: The town holds a music festival every summer.

originalSense.definition: Pertaining to a feast or feast day; festive. (Now only as the noun used attributively.)
originalSense.example: The choir sang a festival hymn during the celebration.

reason: The noun event meaning replaces the historical festive adjective as the learner default.

sense.definition: A reward given to someone who wins a competition or achieves something.
sense.example: She won first prize in the photography competition.

originalSense.definition: That which is taken from another; something captured; a thing seized by force, stratagem, or superior power.
originalSense.example: The captured ship was claimed as a prize after the battle.

reason: Award is the common modern noun meaning; captured booty remains a separate historical sense.

sense.definition: A person who is in or uses a building, room or vehicle.
sense.example: All occupants of the car were wearing seatbelts.

originalSense.definition: A person who occupies an office or a position.
originalSense.example: The current occupant of the post will retire next month.

reason: A person in a place is a more useful general default than an officeholder.

sense.definition: Relating to study, teaching or research in an educational institution.
sense.example: Students need strong academic writing skills for the course.

originalSense.definition: Belonging to the school or philosophy of Plato.
originalSense.example: The scholar examined the academic philosophy associated with Plato.
originalSense.usage: Specialised or historical meaning; this learning example illustrates the existing selected sense, not its most common modern use.

reason: The Platonic philosophy meaning is specialised and historical.

sense.definition: Happening repeatedly at fairly even intervals.
sense.example: Regular exercise can improve your health.

originalSense.definition: Bound by religious rule; belonging to a monastic or religious order (often as opposed to secular).
originalSense.example: The historian compared the duties of regular clergy and secular clergy.

reason: The religious-order meaning should not be the common default.

sense.definition: A room, group of rooms or building where people do administrative or professional work.
sense.example: The company moved into a larger office near the station.

originalSense.definition: A duty or service performed as part of a ceremony, especially a religious ceremony.
originalSense.example: The choir performed its customary office at the ceremony.
originalSense.usage: Specialised or historical meaning; this learning example illustrates the existing selected sense, not its most common modern use.

reason: The ceremonial duty meaning is specialised; workplace is the useful modern meaning.

sense.definition: In the phrase according to: as stated or reported by a person, document or other source.
sense.example: According to the timetable, the next train leaves at noon.
sense.usage: Use according to followed by the source of the information.

originalSense.definition: Bringing things into agreement or harmony; the -ing form of accord.
originalSense.example: The musicians were according their voices to produce a single harmony.
originalSense.usage: Specialised or historical meaning; this learning example illustrates the existing selected sense, not its most common modern use.

reason: The dictionary only has the verb participle, adjective and rare adverb; author a distinct phrase meaning rather than calling the harmony verb common modern English.

sense.definition: Relating to computers and electronic technology.
sense.example: The library provides access to digital resources.

originalSense.definition: Having to do with digits (fingers or toes); especially, performed with a finger.
originalSense.example: The doctor used digital pressure to examine the painful area.
originalSense.usage: Specialised or historical meaning; this learning example illustrates the existing selected sense, not its most common modern use.

reason: The finger-related meaning is specialised; the technology meaning is the modern learning default.

sense.definition: A structure beside the water where boats can be secured and loaded or unloaded.
sense.example: The ferry waited at the dock while passengers boarded.

originalSense.definition: Any of the genus Rumex of coarse weedy plants with small green flowers related to buckwheat, especially bitter dock (Rumex obtusifolius), and used as potherbs and in folk medicine, especially in curing nettle rash.
originalSense.example: Dock grows along the edge of the field.

reason: The plant meaning remains distinct; the waterside structure is more useful for general learners.

sense.definition: To give your full attention to something.
sense.example: I find it easier to concentrate in a quiet room.

originalSense.definition: To bring to, or direct toward, a common center; to unite more closely; to gather into one body, mass, or force.
originalSense.example: The lens concentrates light into a narrow beam.

reason: The scientific gathering meaning is valid, but focusing attention is the more useful general learner default.

sense.definition: A legally established organisation that carries on a business.
sense.example: The company plans to open a new branch next year.

originalSense.definition: A team; a group of people who work together for a common purpose.
originalSense.example: A company of volunteers worked together to restore the hall.
wordFamily: a man is known by the company he keeps
fish and company stink after three days

reason: The business organisation meaning should be learned before the generic company-of-people sense.

sense.definition: A recording of moving images that tells a story or presents information; a movie.
sense.example: We watched a film about life in the Arctic.

originalSense.definition: A thin layer of some substance; a pellicle; a membranous covering, causing opacity.
originalSense.example: A thin film of oil floated on the water.

reason: The thin layer meaning remains useful and separate; the movie meaning is the general learning default.

sense.definition: A section of DNA or RNA that carries hereditary information and influences how an organism develops or functions.
sense.example: Scientists identified a gene linked to the inherited condition.

originalSense.definition: A theoretical unit of heredity of living organisms which may take several values and (in principle) predetermines a precise trait of an organism's form (phenotype), such as hair color.
originalSense.example: A change in a single gene can affect an inherited trait.

reason: The molecular meaning gives a modern scientific account without saying genes necessarily predetermine a precise trait.

sense.definition: Practical judgement based on ordinary experience rather than specialist knowledge.
sense.example: She used commonsense to solve the everyday problem.

originalSense.definition: Practical judgement based on ordinary experience; a form of common sense.
originalSense.example: She used commonsense to solve the everyday problem.

reason: The repaired definition and example describe a noun, so select the actual noun ID instead of the adjective ID.

sense.definition: The exchange of information, ideas or feelings between people or groups.
sense.example: Clear communication between staff and managers prevents misunderstandings.

originalSense.definition: The act or fact of communicating anything; transmission.
originalSense.example: The communication of the disease was reduced by better hygiene.

reason: The disease-transmission example is uncommon; information exchange is the useful modern learning meaning.

sense.definition: The surface of a device on which pictures or information are displayed.
sense.example: The results appeared on the computer screen.

originalSense.definition: A physical barrier that shelters or hides.
originalSense.example: A screen protected the room from the heat of the fire.

reason: The barrier sense is valid but electronic display is the more useful learner default.

sense.definition: A place where goods are sold; a shop.
sense.example: The new store sells books and stationery.

originalSense.definition: A place where items may be accumulated or routinely kept.
originalSense.example: The cellar serves as a store for spare equipment.

reason: The storage-place meaning remains separate; shop is the common learner noun meaning.

sense.definition: The topic being discussed, studied or written about.
sense.example: The subject of the lecture was renewable energy.

originalSense.definition: Likely to be affected by or to experience something; liable.
originalSense.example: The coastal town is subject to frequent storms.
wordFamily: fee simple subject to condition subsequent
fee simple subject to executory interest
fee simple subject to executory limitation

reason: The subject-to adjective is valid but topic is the more useful default for a general word list.

sense.definition: A short account that gives the main points of something.
sense.example: Please write a brief summary of the article.

originalSense.definition: Concise, brief, or presented in a condensed form; presenting information in such a form.
originalSense.example: The document provides a summary account of the findings.

reason: The noun main-points meaning is the common learning target; concise adjective remains separate.

sense.definition: To buy the ownership of a company or another owner's share in it.
sense.example: The investor offered to buy out the other owners of the business.

originalSense.definition: to purchase the entire stock or extent of something
originalSense.example: The investor offered to buy out the other owners of the business.

reason: The existing example illustrates buying ownership, not buying an entire stock of goods.

sense.definition: To begin doing or dealing with an activity or task.
sense.example: She decided to take up swimming to improve her fitness.

originalSense.definition: The act or rate of accepting or using an offer, service or opportunity; a form of take-up.
originalSense.example: The low take up of the offer surprised the organisers.

reason: The space-separated phrasal verb is the useful default; the noun form of take-up remains a separate meaning.

sense.definition: The replacement of old buildings or infrastructure with new ones on the same site.
sense.example: The redevelopment of the old industrial site will create new housing.

originalSense.definition: The process of developing something anew.
originalSense.example: The novel explores the redevelopment of the hero's character.

reason: The urban meaning is the useful learner default; the character-redevelopment example was unnatural.

sense.definition: To want or feel like having or doing something.
sense.example: Do you fancy a cup of tea after the walk?

originalSense.definition: The imagination.
originalSense.example: His fancy supplied imaginary adventures during the long journey.

reason: The imagination noun is chiefly literary; the want-or-feel-like verb is useful in modern British English.
